summary.headline: Brainbees (FirstCry) Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to ₹2,106 crore, but India multi-channel gross margin fell 260 bps YoY, holding adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to ₹2,106 crore, the strongest growth in five years per management, and consolidated loss after tax narrowed 34% YoY. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 4.24% from 4.98%, and gross margin fell to 36.5% from 38.5%. India multi-channel revenue grew about 18%, its fastest in seven quarters, but its gross margin pressure from diapering competition and rupee/crude-linked costs drove the EBITDA margin lower. International and GlobalBees losses narrowed while the school segment grew strongly.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 18% YoY, the strongest in seven quarters, with growth trending up from 7.5% in Q1 FY26 through 7.9%, 8.9%, 11.4%. Gross margin fell about 260 bps YoY (280 bps in Q4), recovering only 20 bps sequentially; EBITDA margin down about 290 bps YoY. GMV grew 12%, orders 12%, AUTC 10%; non-diapering is about 85% of GMV, and offline GMV grew 15%.

segments.name: International (Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 12% YoY, with AUTC up 7% and GMV up 9%. Adjusted EBITDA losses fell 22% YoY; loss as a share of revenue improved to 7% from 10%, and gross margin expanded about 280 bps.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: Revenue was roughly flat, with core categories up 2%, attributed to a planned warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand expected to complete in Q2. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 3.9% from 1%. Management expects growth to recover from Q3; excluding the Flipkart revenue-recognition change, gross margin is similar YoY.

segments.name: Pre-school (FirstCry Intellitots)
segments.commentary: Net revenue rose 47% YoY to ₹19 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 65% to ₹5 crore; EBITDA margin about 26% vs 23% a year earlier. Over 500 pre-schools currently; management targets at least 1,000 over the next couple of years.

guidance_outlook: India multi-channel growth expected to remain elevated over the next few quarters, supported by RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline assortment changes.
Diapering competitive intensity expected to ease; management says it has seen a benign state in July and August and expects a 4-6 quarter normalisation.
Pass-through of rupee depreciation and crude-linked raw material costs in manufacturing expected to be complete by end of Q2 FY27, with full margin recovery from Q3.
Management says the India multi-channel EBITDA margin decline should shrink substantially in H2; it did not give a numerical margin target.
GlobalBees growth expected to bounce back from Q3 FY27 once the brand transition completes in Q2.
Net addition of about 90-100 offline stores in FY27 (net of attrition); FY28 expansion expected to be stronger.
International business targets EBITDA neutrality as soon as possible, but management declined to give a breakeven quarter.
capex_capacity: Offline store expansion of about 90-100 net new stores planned for FY27, after a pause for capital efficiency and product realignment.
RocketBees delivery network expanded from 62 to 72 cities and now handles over 50% of online shipments, with delivery turnaround time about 20% faster.

FC Qwik (2-hour quick delivery) expanded from 5 cities and about 60,000 shipments in March to 12 cities and about 125,000 shipments in June; target of 10% of online shipments, and up to 20% in specific pincodes.
Manufacturing business faces input cost pressure from crude-linked raw materials and rupee depreciation, which is being passed on to customers.
demand_pricing: Diapering (about 15% of India multi-channel business) faced heightened competition from quick commerce players' aggressive pricing, which management says has started to ease, especially in branded diapering.
Non-diapering is about 85% of GMV; fashion is more than 50% of GMV and home brands more than 50% of business, per management.
Non-diapering consumables are about 15% of GMV, with healthy margins per management.
The GMV-to-revenue gap (GMV +12%, revenue +18%) was attributed to the mix of online, offline and manufacturing revenue, plus a GST 2.0 reduction in MRP from Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Jay Laddha asked how much consolidated gross margin recovered in Q1 and the timeline for International breakeven.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the only gross margin gap is India multi-channel, where 20 bps was recovered in Q1 after a 280 bps Q4 loss. International gross margin is improving; no breakeven quarter was given, only input trends (home brand mix, high-margin brands, customer acquisition).

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Kumar asked whether India multi-channel growth can be sustained and when margins will recover.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to remain elevated for the next few quarters. It expects margin recovery to be faster, with the crude/rupee pass-through complete by end Q2 and most of the margin back from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Ranodeep Sen asked about the right to win in diapering and the pre-school M&A plans.
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that diapering competition is driven by retention-poor private labels and quick commerce discounting, and that the category should normalise over a couple of quarters. On pre-school, management said it will grow organically, has no M&A plans yet, and targets at least 1,000 pre-schools in a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki asked whether H2 India multi-channel EBITDA margin would at least match last year and why margin fell sequentially.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 280 bps gross margin decline in Q4 narrowed to 260 bps YoY in Q1; the remaining 30 bps came from logistics costs from RocketBees and FC Qwik, partly offset by marketing and fixed-cost leverage. Management said the YoY margin decline should reduce substantially, without giving a numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Gokal Gandhi asked for the profitability delta between diapering and non-diapering, and the company's diapering share.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delta has widened, that diapering is not loss-making, and that the gap should narrow as diapering margins recover. It did not give a diapering market share figure.

qa_highlights.question: Archana Menon asked for offline KPIs beyond revenue, store expansion plans and the size of non-diapering consumables.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited RocketBees delivery and FC Qwik improvements and offline GMV up 15%. It plans about 90-100 net new stores in FY27. Non-diapering consumables are about 15% of GMV.

risks_watch: India multi-channel gross margin recovery is still only 20 bps of the 280 bps Q4 loss, and management's Q2-Q3 timelines depend on diapering competition easing.
GlobalBees growth depends on completing a brand warehouse and inventory transition in Q2 FY27; management expects growth to bounce back from Q3.
Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East affects International growth; management has not given a breakeven timeline.
Rupee depreciation and crude-linked raw material costs in manufacturing need full pass-through to customers by end Q2 FY27.
Quick commerce and private-label entrants in diapering could keep pricing pressure elevated beyond the expected 4-6 quarter normalisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and recovery in India multi-channel, but evasive on timelines for International breakeven and the margin recovery magnitude. Management repeatedly gave qualitative direction without numerical guidance, and several answers, including on the diapering profitability delta, were non-specific.
key_quotes: Overall business has grown 13% year on year. This is the strongest revenue growth in the last five years, that we have demonstrated on a consolidated basis
This is a temporary and planned transition that should be complete in Q2 and therefore we expect the growth to bounce back starting Q3.
So, I think this is more of a transitory period, nothing structural.

adds.what: Net addition of about 90-100 offline stores in FY27 (net of attrition)

growth.why: Management expects India multi-channel growth to stay elevated through FY27 (Q1 revenue +13% consolidated, India multi-channel ~+18%), backed by RocketBees expansion to 72 cities, FC Qwik scaling from 60k to 125k monthly shipments, and 90-100 net new offline stores in FY27; no numerical revenue guide given and offline store timing is only partly specified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India multi-channel gross margin fell 260 bps YoY and only 20 bps was recovered sequentially from the 280 bps Q4 loss; management expects crude/rupee pass-through complete by end Q2 and most margin back from Q3, though no numerical target was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management plans about 90-100 net new offline stores in FY27 after a pause; RocketBees expanded from 62 to 72 cities and FC Qwik from 5 to 12 cities, with timing only partly specified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India multi-channel revenue grew about 18% (fastest in seven quarters), GMV up 12% and orders up 12%; management says growth stays elevated for subsequent FY27 quarters, though no numerical guide was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was deliberately paused for capital efficiency and product realignment, and utilisation was not disclosed, so no new capex announcement is firmly signalled beyond the store rollout.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave only qualitative direction with no numerical guidance, and margin recovery magnitude and International breakeven timing were left open.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin recovery depends on diapering competition easing (4-6 quarter normalisation) and on full crude/rupee pass-through by end Q2, and GlobalBees growth depends on a Q2 warehouse transition, so slippage is a real risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was discussed; pre-school expansion is to 1,000+ centres over a couple of years, which is network growth rather than a product launch.

rows.label: Crude/rupee cost pass-through to customers
rows.why: Management says all crude-linked and rupee-driven cost increases will be passed on by end Q2, which should lift India multi-channel gross margin back from Q3.

rows.label: GlobalBees growth bounce-back
rows.why: Core categories grew only 2% and revenue was roughly flat while a core brand's warehouse transition completes in Q2; adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 3.9% from 1%.

rows.label: International EBITDA neutrality
rows.why: International loss narrowed to 7% of revenue from 10% and losses fell 22%, but management declined to give a breakeven quarter and cited Middle East disruption.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line momentum and India multi-channel recovery, but cautious and non-specific on the size and timing of margin recovery, International breakeven and the diapering profitability gap; analysts pressed on the margin path and sequential decline.
